articles.title: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Warns India Against Regime Change, Citing Global Political Unrest - Xpert Times
articles.summary: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Warns India Against Regime Change, Citing Global Political Unrest  Xpert Times
articles.full_text:
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat has warned against attempts to bring about what he described as “regime change” in India, referring to political unrest and developments in countries including France, Albania, Bangladesh and Nepal. Speaking at the organisation’s annual Vijayadashami celebrations in Nagpur on October 20, Bhagwat argued that changing a government does not automatically resolve the underlying problems facing a society. His remarks come amid an ongoing political controversy over protests related to the Election Commission and demands for accountability in electoral processes.
Bhagwat’s address focused on national unity, political stability and the importance of ensuring that public movements remain directed towards finding solutions. He suggested that demonstrations could lose their constructive purpose if they became vehicles for personal ambitions, political rivalries or attempts to create hostility between different sections of society.
The RSS chief referred to unrest in several countries to illustrate his concerns. His argument was that political upheavals, leadership changes and public demonstrations do not necessarily deliver the improvements that protesters expect. He maintained that India should not assume that replacing a political establishment would, by itself, address economic, social or institutional challenges.
His comments also reflected the wider debate over the role of public protests in a democracy. Demonstrations are a recognised means through which citizens express dissatisfaction, demand accountability and bring attention to problems that may otherwise receive limited attention. At the same time, questions about public order, political messaging and the consequences of prolonged unrest often become central to debates surrounding major demonstrations.
Bhagwat urged people to ensure that movements remained focused on resolving grievances rather than encouraging hostility. He emphasised the need to respect constitutional principles and maintain appropriate standards of public conduct. His message placed social cohesion and national development at the centre of his argument.
The remarks also included a broader concern about international influences. Bhagwat alleged that external forces could exploit domestic disagreements to weaken countries and advance their own interests. These assertions represent his assessment of international political developments; establishing whether particular foreign actors have influenced events in India would require separate evidence.
The political context is significant because the controversy surrounding the Election Commission has already generated competing interpretations. Critics of electoral processes argue that institutional accountability and transparent procedures are essential to public confidence. Supporters of the government and those echoing Bhagwat’s concerns have warned that some political campaigns may extend beyond their stated objectives.
These positions raise a fundamental question: how should a democracy distinguish between legitimate demands for institutional reform and political efforts intended to destabilise an elected government? The answer depends on the evidence, the methods used by protesters and the constitutional processes available for resolving disputes.
Bhagwat expressed confidence that India would not experience the kind of regime change he associated with unrest abroad. He attributed the country’s resilience to its development, leadership and the growing sense of national responsibility among its people.
However, the strength of democratic institutions also depends on public participation, independent scrutiny and the ability to question those in power. Political stability and accountability are not necessarily opposing objectives; they can reinforce each other when disputes are handled through transparent and lawful processes.
Ultimately, Bhagwat’s speech has added another dimension to the national debate over protests, governance and political change. His central message was that movements should deliver practical solutions rather than deepen social divisions. Whether political leaders, protest organisers and institutions can meet that standard will remain an important test of India’s democratic life.

articles.title: Yogi government’s policies transform UP into an electronics and semiconductor hub - The Times of India
articles.summary: Yogi government’s policies transform UP into an electronics and semiconductor hub  The Times of India

LUCKNOW: Rs 43,000 crore investment and more than 3 lakh employment opportunities generated in electronics sector; more than 55 percent of India’s mobile phones manufactured in Uttar Pradesh.
Semiconductor ecosystem takes shape with Rs 3,700 crore ATMP facility and 1,000-acre semiconductor park. More than 24,000 DPIIT-registered startups and expanding AI, robotics and deep-tech ecosystem strengthen technology-driven growth
Uttar Pradesh is undergoing a significant transformation in its industrial and technology landscape, emerging as an important destination for electronics manufacturing, semiconductors, artificial intelligence, robotics, deep-tech and other future-oriented industries.
Under the leadership of chief minister 
Yogi Adityanath
, the state has sought to move beyond traditional industrial sectors and create an ecosystem where manufacturing, technology, innovation, infrastructure, startups and skilled human resources reinforce one another.
The expansion of the electronics sector is among the clearest indicators of this transformation. Supported by investment-friendly policies, improved infrastructure, better connectivity and a large technical workforce, Uttar Pradesh has developed a substantial electronics manufacturing ecosystem.
More than 200 companies are operating in the electronics sector, with investments exceeding Rs 43,000 crore and more than three lakh employment opportunities generated. This expansion is creating a wider industrial base extending from mobile phones and consumer electronics to components, appliances, drones and emerging technologies.
Mobile manufacturing has emerged as a major pillar of this growth. More than 55 percent of the mobile phones manufactured in the country are now being produced in Uttar Pradesh.
The development is particularly significant because mobile manufacturing has a wide supply chain encompassing components, assembly, testing, packaging, logistics, warehousing, design and associated services. The concentration of manufacturing activity in the state has therefore helped create opportunities beyond the final assembly line and contributed to the emergence of a broader electronics ecosystem.
Two electronics manufacturing clusters have also been developed in the Gautam Buddh Nagar region, reinforcing the state’s position as a major electronics production centre.
The region benefits from its proximity to the National Capital Region, international connectivity, expressways, airports and established industrial infrastructure. The growing concentration of manufacturing units and supporting enterprises is helping create economies of scale and opportunities for ancillary industries.
The electronics ecosystem in Uttar Pradesh is increasingly diversified. Alongside mobile phones, the state is witnessing activity in tablets, laptops, consumer electronics, household appliances, solar cells, defence and logistics drones, robotics and other technology-intensive products.
Companies such as LG, Haier, Dixon, Raphe, Addverb, Samsung and Bhagwati are part of the expanding ecosystem. Their presence reflects the increasing diversity of manufacturing and technology capabilities developing within the state.
Policy support has been an important component of this expansion. The Uttar Pradesh Electronics Components Manufacturing Policy-2025 has been designed to strengthen the state’s position not merely as an assembly destination but also as a location for component manufacturing.
According to the factsheet, investments exceeding Rs 3,800 crore have already been attracted under the policy. The emphasis on components is particularly important because a competitive electronics industry requires a robust domestic supply chain. Greater availability of components, materials, testing facilities and supporting services can reduce dependence on external sources while creating additional opportunities for domestic enterprises.
The next major frontier for Uttar Pradesh is semiconductors. Semiconductors are at the heart of virtually every modern technology, from smartphones and computers to electric vehicles, defence systems, artificial intelligence infrastructure and advanced industrial machinery. Recognising the strategic importance of this sector, the state is now positioning itself to participate in India’s emerging semiconductor ecosystem.
Under the Central Government’s Semicon India Programme 2.0, with a financial outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore, efforts are being made to build a resilient semiconductor ecosystem in the country. Uttar Pradesh has already secured an important position in this emerging landscape.
A semiconductor ATMP, or Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging, facility has been approved by the Central Government. Operated by India Chip Private Limited, the facility is located in Sector-28 of the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority area and represents an investment of more than Rs3,700 crore.
The importance of such a facility extends beyond the investment itself. Semiconductor manufacturing involves a complex chain of activities, and assembly, testing and packaging are essential stages in converting semiconductor devices into usable components. The establishment of such capabilities can encourage the development of suppliers, specialised logistics, testing services, engineering companies and skilled technical manpower around the facility.
The proposed 1,000-acre semiconductor park in the Yamuna Expressway region further strengthens this long-term vision. The availability of a dedicated industrial area can provide space for semiconductor-related companies, component manufacturers, suppliers, research facilities and other technology enterprises. With the semiconductor industry requiring specialised infrastructure and a reliable ecosystem, the planned park can become an important anchor for technology-intensive industrial development in the region.
Uttar Pradesh is also building capabilities in semiconductor design and associated technologies. The presence of companies and technology organisations such as NXP, Renesas, Qualcomm and Cadence adds another dimension to the state’s emerging semiconductor ecosystem.
The development of design, engineering, packaging, testing and related activities can create opportunities for highly skilled employment and encourage greater interaction between industry, educational institutions and startups.
Infrastructure is another important factor behind the state’s technology ambitions. Technology-intensive industries require reliable transport networks, airports, industrial land, power, digital infrastructure and efficient movement of goods. Uttar Pradesh has substantially expanded its connectivity network, including expressways and dedicated freight corridors.
The Jewar International Airport, the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor and Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, together with the state’s extensive expressway network, are strengthening the logistics foundation required for high-value manufacturing.
The technology ecosystem is also expanding into artificial intelligence and robotics. The 75-acre Robotics and AI Computing Park in Greater Noida represents an effort to develop infrastructure for emerging technologies alongside conventional electronics manufacturing.
The convergence of electronics, computing, AI and robotics is increasingly important because modern manufacturing itself is becoming more automated and data-driven. The presence of robotics and AI capabilities can therefore support both technology startups and established manufacturing companies.
Greater Noida and the wider Gautam Buddh Nagar region are emerging as important nodes in this technology network, while Lucknow is developing as another major centre. The broader objective is to create a technology corridor connecting different strengths of the state rather than concentrating all technology activity in a single location.
The information technology sector provides another important layer to this ecosystem. Investments exceeding Rs7,000 crore have been recorded under the IT Policy. The 100-acre HCL IT City in Lucknow and seven STPI IT Parks across the state are contributing to the expansion of IT-related activities. These facilities provide opportunities for software development, IT services, technology companies and skilled employment while creating links between traditional IT services and newer technology sectors.
Data infrastructure is also becoming increasingly important as the state expands its digital economy. According to the factsheet, investments of more than Rs 21,000 crore have been recorded in the data centre sector. Data centres provide the digital infrastructure required by cloud computing, artificial intelligence, financial technology, e-commerce, enterprise applications and a wide range of digital services. Their growth can therefore complement the development of AI, deep-tech and electronics industries.
A rapidly expanding startup ecosystem is adding an innovation dimension to this transformation. Uttar Pradesh now has more than 24,000 DPIIT-registered startups.
This represents a substantial expansion in entrepreneurial activity and creates a base from which technology-focused enterprises can emerge. The state’s startup ecosystem is increasingly moving beyond conventional service-sector businesses towards deep-tech and innovation-driven enterprises.
The Uttar Pradesh Startup Policy-2026 and U-Hub centres in Noida and Lucknow are aimed at strengthening this ecosystem. articles.title: Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka Participates in the 12th EU–Sri Lanka Inter-Parliamentary Meeting in Belgium - Colombo Gazette
articles.summary: Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka Participates in the 12th EU–Sri Lanka Inter-Parliamentary Meeting in Belgium  Colombo Gazette
articles.full_text:
News, International
20 Oct, 2026
Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka Dr. Jagath Wickramaratne and Deputy Minister of Economic Development, Nishantha Jayaweera, visited Brussels, Belgium, from 13 to 15 October 2026 to participate in the 12th European Union (EU)–Sri Lanka Inter-Parliamentary Meeting (IPM) and engage in bilateral discussions.
The visit commenced with participation in “An Evening in Ceylon,” a tourism promotional event organised by the Embassy of Sri Lanka in Belgium in collaboration with Emirates and Jetwing Travels Sri Lanka at the Sri Lanka Residence in Brussels on 13 October 2026.
The 12th EU–Sri Lanka IPM was co-chaired by the Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka, Dr. Jagath Wickramaratne, and Chair of the European Parliament’s Delegation for Relations with the Countries of South Asia, Șerban-Dimitrie Sturdza and concluded successfully on 15 October 2026. Deputy Minister of Economic Development, Nishantha Jayaweera; Ambassador of Sri Lankato Belgium, Luxembourg and the European Union Chandana Weerasena; and senior officials of the Embassy of Sri Lanka in Brussels were also part of the Sri Lankan delegation.
As the first EU–Sri Lanka IPM following the formation of Sri Lanka’s 10th Parliament, the meeting marked an important milestone in parliamentary relations between the two sides and reaffirmed their commitment
to strengthening dialogue and cooperation.
The meeting provided a platform to discuss a broad range of issues of mutual interest, including political and economic relations, GSP+, good governance, the rule of law, trade, investment, sustainable development, connectivity and people-to-people links. Discussions also covered regional and international developments, including the situations in Ukraine and the Middle East, the Indo-Pacific region and maritime cooperation.
Co-Chair Șerban-Dimitrie Sturdza and Members of the European Parliament acknowledged Sri Lanka’s resilience in addressing multiple challenges, including the impact of Cyclone Ditwah and the energy crisis arising from unrest in the Middle East, and commended the country’s positive economic growth trajectory.
Co-Chair Dr. Jagath Wickramaratne expressed appreciation for the European Union’s financial and humanitarian assistance to Sri Lanka following Cyclone Ditwah, including emergency relief supplies, disaster assessment support and recovery efforts. He also acknowledged the EU’s continued support during challenging periods, particularly Sri Lanka’s engagement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Paris Club debt restructuring process, and requested further assistance to strengthen economic relations amid ongoing geopolitical challenges.
Highlighting the significant development of EU–Sri Lanka relations under the 1995 EU–Sri Lanka Cooperation Agreement, Dr. Wickramaratne emphasised the importance of elevating the partnership to the next level. Both sides recognised the European Union’s role as a major export market and development partner for Sri Lanka and underscored the importance of continued parliamentary engagement in advancing shared priorities.
During the visit, Dr. Wickramaratne held a series of high-level meetings, including discussions with the Vice-President of the European Parliament, Younous Omarjee, on bilateral relations, regular engagement mechanisms and areas for further cooperation. The European Parliament’s Delegation for Relations with the Countries of South Asia also arranged a tour of the European Parliament for the Sri Lankan delegation, which included observing a committee meeting. In addition, Co-Chair Șerban-Dimitrie Sturdza and Members of the European Parliament hosted an official dinner for the Sri Lankan delegation.
The Speaker also visited the Federal Parliament of Belgium, where he met the President of the Chamber of Representatives, Peter De Roover and other members of the Chamber. He outlined Sri Lanka’s political stability, ongoing economic recovery and the Government’s efforts to transform the country’s political, economic and social landscape following the public mandate received at the 2024 Presidential and Parliamentary elections.
Dr. Wickramaratne thanked the Belgian Government for its cooperation and requested a senior-level bilateral visit from Belgium to Sri Lanka. Such a visit would further strengthen bilateral relations as the two countries prepare to commemorate the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2028. The delegation also undertook a study tour of the Federal Parliament of Belgium.
Minister, Madusanka Jayasinghe; Minister (Commercial) Thavishya Mullegamgoda; and Minister of the Embassy of Sri Lanka in Belgium, Dilini Lenagala, were also part of the Sri Lankan delegation.

articles.title: High Inflation, costlier crude threaten festive demand and corporate margins - cfo.economictimes.indiatimes.com
articles.summary: High Inflation, costlier crude threaten festive demand and corporate margins  cfo.economictimes.indiatimes.com
articles.full_text:
Rising inflation, elevated crude oil prices and currency volatility are emerging as risks to consumption and investment in India, economists said, warning that the combination could weigh on demand and squeeze corporate margins.
Brent crude, the international benchmark, traded above $109 a barrel on Tuesday as investors weighed escalating conflicts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe against strong Persian Gulf energy flows.
Currency markets have also been volatile, with the Indian rupee weakening to ₹96.85 per US dollar on October 7. Following market operations by the Reserve Bank of India to stabilise the currency, the rupee was trading at ₹94.93 per dollar on Tuesday.
Economists said India is better placed to weather the uncertainty than several emerging and developed economies, supported by domestic consumption, fiscal prudence and strong corporate balance sheets.
However, for Indian businesses, the combination of risks poses a serious threat to demand as well as margins.
The immediate concern for India Inc is whether higher prices will weaken consumer spending in the second half of the financial year.
Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, said GDP growth is expected to be around 7.2% in FY27, with much of it supported by the performance in the first two quarters. Growth in the third and fourth quarters, however, will depend considerably on consumption.
Sabnavis said the festive season would be a crucial test of demand. Companies may be reluctant to raise prices significantly for fear of hurting sales, but absorbing some of the increase in input costs could put pressure on margins.
Inflation and borrowing costs threaten household spending
Further increases in interest rates remain a risk if inflationary and geopolitical pressures persist. The extent of any future monetary tightening will depend on the RBI’s assessment of the inflation outlook and its policy decisions.
“Household disposable incomes would be further impinged by the increase in interest rates as households having floating-rate mortgages would have to pay higher EMIs. New consumption loans will become more expensive and the ability of households to borrow and service mortgages and consumption loans at those rates will also be constrained,” Banerjee said.
The impact on demand is likely to be broad-based, Banerjee said, although essential categories such as food, transport and medicines, along with premium and luxury products, could be relatively better placed.
For companies, the challenge will be to balance cost recovery against the risk of losing sales. Sabnavis said the extent to which manufacturers pass on higher input costs would become clearer in the current quarter.
“Margins will need to be watched closely. If companies are unable to pass on higher input costs to consumers, their margins will come under pressure,” he said.
Elevated crude prices and currency volatility could make that trade-off more difficult, particularly for businesses dependent on imported inputs.
Higher rates could weigh on private capex
According to RBI’s September Bulletin, capital expenditure by India’s private corporate sector is estimated at ₹3.2 lakh crore in FY27, compared with ₹2.6 lakh crore in FY26. The estimate is based on the pipeline of ongoing projects financed through banks and financial institutions, external commercial borrowings and initial public offerings.
Sabnavis said that investment will remain strong, although concentrated in a limited number of sectors.
“Investment decisions are based on long-term considerations, not merely on what is happening today. Investment will continue to be strong this year, but it will not be broad-based,” he said, pointing to data centres, power, machinery, metals and refineries as key drivers.
Banerjee, however, cautioned that sustained inflation and higher interest rates could weaken demand and reduce industrial capacity utilisation, prompting companies to defer investment decisions.
He also highlighted a policy dilemma for the RBI. Inflation is being driven by supply-side pressures rather than excess demand, but the central bank’s inflation-targeting mandate could require monetary tightening. This could further weaken consumption and investment even as businesses continue to face elevated input costs.
Banerjee added that a quick resolution of the ongoing conflicts could ease inflationary pressures.

articles.title: Bhagwat asserts regime change operations cannot succeed in India - The Siasat Daily
articles.summary: Bhagwat asserts regime change operations cannot succeed in India  The Siasat Daily

Mumbai: In a direct address to ongoing political agitations across the country, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat declared on Tuesday, October 20, that attempts to force a “regime change” in India will fail.
Delivering his annual Vijayadashami address in Nagpur, the RSS chief emphasised that public movements must aim to resolve issues rather than stoke social animosity or serve short-term electoral gains. His remarks came in the backdrop of recent anti-Election Commission demonstrations and persistent calls by political opponents demanding systemic overhauls.
Drawing explicit comparisons to recent geopolitical upheavals, Bhagwat pointed to violent unrest and political instability observed across several foreign nations. “A storm has blown in the West. Look at what transpired in France, Bangladesh, and Nepal,” Bhagwat stated, warning against similar foreign or domestic tactics inside India. “Regime change will not happen in India. Such attempts continue in India as well. India has moved forward with steadfast resolve, and the collective vitality (purushartha) of its society has grown.”
He cautioned that engineered agitations that aim to dislodge elected systems under the guise of public protest do not solve fundamental problems, noting that changing regimes does not automatically fix societal challenges.
While acknowledging that public discontent and organised protests are natural components of a functioning democracy, the RSS leader insisted that movements must remain within the “boundaries of propriety” (mariyada). “Movements must be directed exclusively towards finding constructive solutions rather than causing friction. Public demonstrations must not sow hatred or hostility among different sections of society. Agitations guided purely by the pursuit of votes or cheap popularity harm long-term stability,” said Bhagwat.
He further added, “Lasting solutions do not emerge from continuous protest alone, but through mutual discourse and constructive dialogue within society.
“Problems arise, and movements take shape; however, these should be directed towards finding solutions. The primary objective must be a resolution,” Bhagwat noted, urging political parties and movement leaders to prioritise social harmony over political opportunism.
Bhagwat outlined a strong vision for national integration and global leadership. Emphasising the distinction between eternal values and evolving societal dynamics, Bhagwat urged citizens to ground themselves in ‘Svabodh’ (self-awareness) while adapting flexibly to modern challenges.
The RSS chief stressed that while diversity is dynamic, the underlying principle of unity in India remains eternal and immutable.
Referring to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution –“We, the People of India” — he highlighted that emotional integration lies at the heart of Indian society. He noted that forgetting these core values and losing sight of right conduct historically weakened the nation, leading to foreign subjugation.
Reflecting on the sacrifices made by freedom fighters for the nation’s independence, the RSS chief stated that safeguarding India’s identity and sovereignty today demands an even greater commitment. He placed the responsibility of steering India towards becoming a global leader (Vishwaguru) squarely on the shoulders of the younger generation.
Addressing recent natural calamities, including environmental disruptions in Nepal and across the Himalayan belt, Bhagwat cautioned against unbridled development. He warned against development models that disregard ecological balance, stating that progress must be inclusive and sustainable rather than destructive to human existence.
Highlighting growing geopolitical conflicts across the globe, Bhagwat asserted that India holds the ideological answers to world peace. On technological advancements, he acknowledged the benefits of information accessibility but emphasised the necessity of critical thinking, moral discretion, and wisdom. He urged governments and administrative bodies to carefully regulate information channels to ensure public safety and accurate information flow.
Reaffirming the country’s ancient traditions, Bhagwat noted that India’s strength lies in accepting, respecting, and embracing diverse languages, castes, regional cultures, and customs. He concluded that the flexibility inherent in the Sanatan tradition provides the foundation for harmonious co-existence.
“The principle of unity is eternal and unshakeable, whereas our diversity is dynamic. Flexibility in diversity is the hallmark of Sanatan philosophy. The responsibility to make India a Vishwaguru now rests on the shoulders of the new generation,” he remarked.

Furthermore, the Russian diplomat highlighted how frequent border post closures severely disrupt essential regional trade and transit commerce.
Addressing the same event, Pakistani Ambassador to Russia Faisal Niaz Tirmizi welcomed expanding bilateral security cooperation with Moscow. Tirmizi pointed to recent high-level law enforcement visits as positive momentum for joint counterterrorism efforts between both nations. He stressed the importance of translating political goodwill into practical partnerships across defense, security, and intelligence sectors. Consequently, enhanced security coordination aims to stabilize volatile border regions and protect crucial economic corridors from violent extremism.
To boost bilateral trade, Ambassador Tirmizi called for direct commercial flights and simplified visa processing for citizens. He urged both governments to establish efficient banking mechanisms that resolve ongoing international payment and transaction constraints. He also cautioned against movements driven primarily by electoral calculations or the pursuit of popularity, stressing that lasting solutions required discussion and mutual understanding.
“Movements alone do not provide solutions; true solutions emerge from dialogue and mutual discourse within society,” Bhagwat said.
He further warned against groups seeking to create discontent and disorder by encouraging a sense of victimhood among people. Bhagwat urged citizens to remain vigilant against attempts to deepen divisions and create confusion within society.

Bhagwat also stressed the importance of national unity while recognising India's religious and cultural diversity. He said differences in religious practices and beliefs should not become grounds for social separation.
Urging people to move beyond personal egos and misconceptions about their own and others' forms of worship, he highlighted devotion to the country, pride in its ancestors and commitment to Indian culture as common bonds that could strengthen society.
The RSS chief called for collective efforts towards national progress, saying India should continue working towards its aspiration of becoming a “Vishwaguru”, or a global leader, while preserving social harmony and mutual goodwill.

articles.title: Marco Rubio To Visit India Today: What’s At Stake? - Outlook India
articles.summary: Marco Rubio To Visit India Today: What’s At Stake?  Outlook India
articles.full_text:
- Marco Rubio is meeting External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai, with energy, trade, investment, defence and emerging technologies on the agenda.
- The visit comes as India and the US work towards a trade agreement amid tensions over tariffs and New Delhi’s purchases of Russian crude oil.
- Rubio’s schedule includes meetings with business leaders and a visit to Reliance Industries’ Jamnagar refinery, highlighting the commercial and energy dimensions of the relationship.
Diplomacy often begins with a list of subjects both sides agree to discuss. The harder question is what happens when those conversations take place against a backdrop of tariffs, visa restrictions and disagreements over energy. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to India brings that tension into focus, with trade, energy security, defence and critical technologies set to feature in talks with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai on Tuesday, October 20. The meeting comes as New Delhi and Washington try to stabilise a relationship strained by President Donald Trump’s tariff threats and differences over India’s purchases of Russian oil.
Rubio’s India leg runs from October 20 to 22, taking him to Mumbai and Jamnagar in Gujarat rather than New Delhi. His schedule combines official diplomacy with business outreach, reflecting the commercial stakes of the relationship. The visit is also an opportunity to prepare for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s expected trip to the United States for the G20 leaders’ summit in December.
What Is On Rubio’s Schedule?
Rubio is expected to arrive in Mumbai on Tuesday afternoon, with the schedule placing his meeting with Jaishankar at around 4 pm. The discussions are expected to cover energy, trade and investment, defence, and critical and emerging technologies, according to the Ministry of External Affairs. The meeting is intended to review the wider India-US strategic partnership at a time when both governments have reasons to keep diplomatic channels open.
The Mumbai programme also includes a visit to the Taj Mahal Palace hotel, where Rubio is expected to pay tribute at the memorial to the victims of the November 2008 Mumbai terror attacks. Later, he and Jaishankar are scheduled to attend an event marking the 250th anniversary of American independence, with the Indian foreign minister as guest of honour. The schedule combines remembrance with a public demonstration of the diplomatic relationship the two countries are seeking to sustain.
On Wednesday, October 21, Rubio is expected to meet Indian business executives, institutional investors and banking officials in Mumbai. The discussions are expected to focus on investment, trade and supply chains. On Thursday, October 22, he is scheduled to travel to Jamnagar to visit Reliance Industries’ refining and petrochemical complex before concluding his India programme. The refinery visit places energy and commercial cooperation at the centre of the trip, rather than treating them as subjects confined to government meeting rooms.
Trade, Russian Oil And The Tariff Dispute
The economic relationship is one of the most immediate tests facing the two sides. Trade negotiations have continued amid uncertainty over US tariffs on Indian goods, while Washington has pressed countries buying Russian energy through the threat of punitive measures. India, which relies heavily on imported crude oil, has argued that its energy choices must account for domestic demand and national energy security. Rubio’s visit comes after the US passed legislation authorising steep tariffs on buyers of Russian energy, leaving India concerned about the possible consequences for trade and its wider relationship with Washington.
A trade agreement is therefore an important part of the backdrop. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor has recently described progress in the negotiations as rapid, while Rubio has said the deal is close to being finalised. Those statements signal momentum, but they do not mean a final agreement has been announced. The talks will need to reconcile differences over market access and the terms governing trade between the two economies.
Energy cooperation offers a possible area of common ground. The United States wants to expand commercial ties with India, including energy supplies, while India seeks reliable sources to meet the needs of its growing economy. A visit to Jamnagar, home to one of the world’s largest refining complexes, gives that discussion a tangible setting. Yet greater American energy sales would supplement a much wider supply mix; they would not automatically settle the dispute over India’s Russian oil purchases.
Defence, Technology And The Wider Strategic Partnership
Beyond trade and oil, the two governments are expected to discuss defence cooperation and critical technologies. India has sought greater technology transfer and opportunities for domestic manufacturing in defence purchases, while both countries have an interest in resilient supply chains for strategically important technologies. Cooperation in emerging fields could help broaden the relationship beyond immediate trade disputes, although the details of any new arrangements will depend on what the talks produce.
Visa restrictions are another source of friction. India has repeatedly highlighted the contribution of Indian professionals and businesses to the US economy, while changes to American immigration policy have raised concerns among skilled workers and companies. The issue sits alongside tariffs and energy as a reminder that the partnership is not free of disagreements, even where the two sides share strategic interests.
Rubio’s visit comes at a moment when both governments have reasons to keep negotiations moving. India has said the first phase of a bilateral trade agreement has been finalised and is undergoing legal drafting, while Trump’s decision to waive key Russia-related tariffs and sanctions has eased an immediate source of pressure on New Delhi. Whether the visit produces further progress on trade, energy or technology will depend on the details agreed by both sides. For now, the schedule offers an opportunity to steady a relationship that remains strategically important but has been tested by disagreements over tariffs and Russian oil.

articles.title: Kim Jong Un photos released to dismiss rumours of coma, takeover by sister - The Times of India
articles.summary: Kim Jong Un photos released to dismiss rumours of coma, takeover by sister  The Times of IndiaKim Jong Un: Why do rumours about his death keep coming back?  BBCKim Jong-un dead or alive: Who will take North Korea leadership in case of death of country's supreme lead  The Economic TimesNorth Korea's 'Proof Of Life' Amid Kim Jong Un 'Brain Haemorrhage Death' Rumour  NDTVKim Jong Un appears at clothing expo after latest internet rumors on death  NK ...
articles.full_text:
North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media, inspecting children's footwear and women's clothing, after unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.
The photographs, published by North Korea's official media on Monday, show Kim examining footwear, gesturing towards officials and inspecting coats at a garment and footwear exhibition. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis in the secretive country, the New York Post reported.
According to North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency, Kim toured the exhibition on Monday. However, the photographs have not been independently authenticated, and it remains unclear precisely when they were taken.
One image shows Kim bending forward to inspect a small pink shoe held by a woman. In another, he gestures with his arms outstretched as he appears to address an official. A third photograph captures him reaching towards the sleeve of a woman's coat displayed on a mannequin.
How the death rumours began
The speculation gathered pace after Wanjun Xie, a US-based Chinese dissident associated with the China Democracy Party, posted a series of claims on X alleging that Kim had died and that his sister, 
Kim Yo Jong
, had taken control of the country.
In a post on Monday, Xie wrote: "Rumours of the death of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un have been circulating online for days, but Kim Jong Un has not yet made a public appearance to deny them. This indirectly confirms that the rumours of Kim Jong Un's death are likely true. Furthermore, it is rumoured that after Kim Jong-un's death, the North Korean regime has not been transferred to his daughter Kim Ju-ae, but is currently in the hands of his sister Kim Yo-jong.
"After assuming power, Kim Yo-jong immediately activated loudspeaker broadcasts to South Korea and fired 201 warning shots. She also warned South Korea that North Korea was considering a comprehensive upgrade of its tactical strike capabilities. This sudden intensification of threats against South Korea is clearly aimed at strengthening her control over the North Korean military and consolidating her power through strong external threats. This indirectly confirms the rumors that Kim Jong-un is dead and that Kim Yo-jong is currently in control of the regime; these rumors are likely true."
The New York Post reported that Xie's claims began gaining traction on Sunday. However, the allegations have not been supported by medical records, identifiable witnesses or other independently verifiable evidence.
In another post on Sunday, Xie claimed that Kim had suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage, fallen into a coma and been transferred to Beijing for emergency treatment. He alleged that a team of specialists from Peking Union Medical College Hospital had travelled to North Korea before Kim was moved to China.
"It is rumoured that recently, Kim Jong-un, General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and Supreme Leader of North Korea, suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage and fell into a coma. Although a team of medical experts from Peking Union Medical College Hospital was dispatched to North Korea to assist in his treatment, the poor medical conditions in North Korea forced Kim Jong-un to be transferred to Peking Union Medical College Hospital for emergency treatment. However, due to the severity of his condition and the fact that the optimal window for treatment had passed, Kim Jong-un succumbed to his injuries and died. His body has been secretly transported back to North Korea, and the news of his death is being kept under wraps."
Xie further alleged that Kim's body had been secretly returned to North Korea and that authorities were concealing news of his death. He also claimed that Chinese troops had been deployed to Pyongyang amid fears of a succession crisis.
In a separate post, he wrote: "It is said that on October 17, Peking Union Medical College Hospital dispatched a team of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular medical experts to North Korea to participate in the rescue of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, who was in critical condition."
Claims of Chinese troop deployment
Xie's posts also fuelled speculation about a possible power struggle involving Kim's daughter, Kim Ju-ae, and his sister, Kim Yo Jong. He claimed that China had sent 9,000 troops to Pyongyang to help stabilise the situation.
The claims of Kim's death, a Chinese troop deployment and a possible succession crisis remain unverified. North Korean authorities have not explicitly addressed the death reports.
What is known about Kim's health?
Kim's health has long been the subject of international speculation. The New York Post reported that South Korea's National Intelligence Service told lawmakers on September 30 that Kim weighed approximately 140 kilograms (309 pounds) and faced an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease because of severe obesity.
However, the agency reportedly detected no significant signs of ill health, pointing to Kim's ability to run up stairs during an inspection of a naval destroyer.
The latest rumours echo a false alarm in 2020, when Ji Seong-ho, a North Korean defector who later became a South Korean lawmaker, claimed he was "99%" certain that Kim had died following cardiovascular surgery. Kim subsequently appeared in public, and Ji apologised for making the erroneous claim.
The New York Post said it had sought comment from the governments of North Korea and China, as well as Peking Union Medical College Hospital.

Welcome to Mumbai, Secretary Rubio, the US embassy in India posted on social media shortly after the top American diplomat landed at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International airport in India's financial capital.

"Discussions are expected to cover key areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade and investment, defence, critical and emerging technologies, and other areas of mutual interest," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said last week.

Washington's new immigration policy and its decision to increase the H1B visa fee also contributed to the slide in India-US ties.

Tehran [Iran], October 20 (ANI): Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on Monday accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of deliberately derailing peace negotiations with Moscow, claiming that Zelenskyy fears any agreement acceptable to both Russia and the United States would result in his personal downfall and the collapse of his government.
Speaking at a press conference following the ninth Russia-Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Joint Ministerial Meeting for Strategic Dialogue, Lavrov alleged that Kyiv had repeatedly undermined diplomatic momentum fostered by Washington.
'We can draw only one conclusion: Zelensky does not want negotiations. He has derailed them repeatedly, apparently because he understands that any agreement acceptable to Russia and the US would spell the end of his regime and of him personally,' Lavrov said, according to the remarks shared by the Russian Ministry of Foriegn Affairs.
Detailing how prior diplomatic efforts broke down, the Russian top diplomat noted that whenever Washington and Moscow reached preliminary understandings on resuming peace talks, Ukraine launched provocations to abort the process.
'On numerous occasions, including several instances when proposals by US President Donald Trump led Moscow and Kyiv to an understanding that we needed to move forward, with some common ground on resuming talks, Ukraine invariably did something utterly unacceptable and abhorrent the very next day after such optimistic expectations emerged,' Lavrov explained. 'Above all, this meant strikes on civilian targets.'
Lavrov also forcefully dismissed European and Ukrainian criticism regarding direct energy negotiations between Moscow and Washington, firmly rejecting claims that Russian fuel exports require approval from Kyiv.
'The 'diesel deal' between Moscow and Washington is a matter for Moscow and Washington,' Lavrov said. 'If the EU regards it as a betrayal of Ukraine, while Zelensky himself claims that Russian diesel exports must be agreed with him because only he can authorise them, then this is no longer a matter of energy security, but of self-promotion and yet another clown show.'
Turning to security concerns in West Asia, Lavrov expressed concern over rising tensions in and around the Strait of Hormuz, calling for efforts to address the underlying causes of the crisis and prevent a renewed military confrontation.
'We must address the root causes of the situation in and around the Strait of Hormuz, including by implementing the agreements reached between US and Iran under the so-called Islamabad Memorandum, which we all welcomed,' Lavrov stated. 'We believe this memorandum still contains everything needed to pull the situation back from the brink of a resumption of full-scale war and return it to the path of political and diplomatic engagement and negotiations.'
To prevent further escalation, Lavrov urged the establishment of a broad, inclusive regional security architecture encompassing both Arab states and Iran, alongside key neighbours such as Iraq and Jordan.
'This should be supported by external actors guided primarily by the interests of the countries of the region, rather than their own unilateral geopolitical designs,' Lavrov noted, adding that Russia remains ready to align its long-standing Collective Security Concept for the Persian Gulf Region with parallel security initiatives proposed by China, Iran, and the GCC.
On the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Lavrov affirmed that both Moscow and its Gulf partners expressed firm opposition to efforts undermining the establishment of an independent Palestinian nation.
'We discussed the Palestinian issue at length. Everyone is deeply concerned by attempts to put an end to the prospect of establishing a Palestinian State. Both we and our GCC partners categorically reject this approach,' he asserted.
Lavrov also thanked Gulf countries for their position on the Russia-Ukraine conflict and their mediation efforts on humanitarian issues, including the reunification of children with their families, prisoner-of-war exchanges and the return of the remains of those killed.
'We thanked our colleagues for their balanced, objective position on Ukraine and briefed them on how the situation is developing at this stage,' Lavrov said. 'We expressed particular gratitude for the efforts of a number of Gulf countries that pragmatically and without publicity mediate on a range of humanitarian issues, including reuniting children with their families, exchanging POWs and returning the bodies of those killed.'
Highlighting economic ties between Russia and the Gulf bloc, Lavrov said bilateral trade had increased by 45 per cent in 2025 to nearly USD 19 billion, adding that there was considerable scope for further growth.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump on Sunday (local time) claimed that negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict were making 'great progress', while defending his administration's diplomatic approach towards Moscow and accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of failing to secure a better deal two years ago.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump described his strategy to strike a deal between the warring nations as a simple one which he said includes ensuring that Russia is not, 'foolishly', driven away from the bargaining table.
This comes as Trump has waived several sanctions related to Russian fuel sales that were to take effect under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a month after signing the Bill.
The legislation would have authorised tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods imported into the United States from the five largest importers of Russian-origin crude oil or natural gas, including India and China.
The decision comes amid a reported diesel supply agreement with Russia, as fuel prices in the United States remain a concern ahead of the November midterm elections.

However, last week, just days before the legislation was due to go into effect, Trump signed an executive order pausing the sanctions.
Rubio: Trade deal ‘very close’
Before traveling to India, Rubio was in Uzbekistan for a meeting of the “C5+1” diplomatic platform comprising the US and five Central Asian countries. In remarks on the sidelines, Rubio said trade talks with India are taking place with the sanctions waivers in mind.
“We have had to waive sanctions over the past few months, looking at the global supplies, looking at global prices, and the impact it was having on other countries,” he said.
READ: Rubio open to Russia, China meets on PH visit
“We’re trying to finalize a trade deal with India right now. We’re very close to doing that,” Rubio added.
In an interview with Indian broadcaster NDTV, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said that Jamnagar could be a valuable source of diesel for the US.
Foreign policy analyst C Raja Mohan of Jindal Global University in India told DW that Rubio skipping a visit to the Indian capital in favor of Mumbai and Jamnagar should not be considered a diplomatic snub, as the refinery has international importance amid the global energy crunch brought on by the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East.
He said Jamnagar is an “important node in global trade” because it processes Russian oil and serves as a conduit for refined Russian petroleum products reaching Western markets.
Although Trump’s sanctions reprieve offers New Delhi temporary relief, the underlying threat remains. Washington retains the option of imposing punitive tariffs, leaving Russian oil as a potential source of leverage in wider trade negotiations.
Former Indian ambassador to the US, Meera Shankar, cautioned against reading too much into Rubio’s decision to skip Delhi amid political criticism in India.
“The focus of his current trip is on energy, and he is visiting the Reliance refinery in Jamnagar,” she told DW. “The high price of fuel, particularly diesel, has become a political liability for the Trump administration, which wants to be seen taking action on this issue.”
Diesel prices have skyrocketed around the world following the Iran war and the ensuing disruption of supply from the Middle East. In waiving Russia sanctions, Trump has tried to blame Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil facilities as being the cause of high prices.
Shankar pointed to Reliance’s proposed Texas refinery, noting that the state is “one of the states in play” in the upcoming midterm elections in the US.
“Some forward movement on the investment would be welcome,” she said.
Trump eroding trust in Delhi?
The two governments continue to describe their ties as a comprehensive global strategic partnership spanning defence, trade, technology and energy.
Analyst Mohan argued that describing the US-India relationship as uniquely transactional was misleading.
“Every nation ultimately acts out of national self-interest, rather than pure altruism or shared values,” he said.
The current friction, in his view, is part of a normal negotiation between two sovereign powers, not proof that the partnership was failing.
Besides Russian oil, another potential area of complication is the Trump administration suspending a scheme allowing US companies to sponsor skilled foreign workers.
On October 8, the Trump administration suspended new and pending applications under the US Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program at several technology companies amid investigations into alleged visa fraud and the displacement of US workers.
The process is a key step for employers seeking permanent residency for foreign staff, including Indian professionals.
Harsh Pant, vice president for studies and foreign policy at the Delhi-based Observer Research Foundation (ORF), said Trump’s own words and actions had damaged ties despite regular high-level engagement.
“Even as he calls Prime Minister Modi a good friend, he has damaged the relationship by targeting India, and his supporters have been targeting Indians,” Pant told DW.
Pant said inconsistent messaging from Washington was eroding trust and could have consequences well beyond Trump’s presidency.
“The sense that America is unreliable, that America can’t be trusted, is beginning to come back into policy discourse,” he said.
The damage, he warned, could reach beyond government-to-government relations to Indian students, professionals and the middle class, whose goodwill has helped sustain ties through earlier disagreements.
“If public sentiment goes against a country, then it becomes very difficult for the policy-makers to craft an alternative policy,” Pant said, adding that US actions affecting Indian students and professionals “will have consequences.” /dl

articles.summary: Donald Trump approval hits record low of 31% as midterms near, Democrats lead by 12 points  The Times of IndiaEXCLUSIVE: Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds  ReutersPoll: Americans are anxious, pessimistic and deeply unhappy with Trump ahead of the midterms  NBC NewsTrump’s approval ratings plummet: what that means for the US midterms  Al JazeeraDonald Trump's approval rating hits new low as Iran war shape...
articles.full_text:
US President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to a record low of 31%, with rising gasoline prices and concerns over the economy weighing on public sentiment ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that concluded on Monday.
The four-day survey found that Trump's approval rating dropped by one percentage point from two weeks earlier, marking the lowest level of either of his presidential terms. The poll also showed Democrats opening a 12-point lead over Republicans among registered voters, the widest margin recorded during the current election cycle.
Asked which party they would support if congressional elections were held today, 47% of registered voters chose Democrats, compared with 35% who backed Republicans.
The Democratic lead has widened from seven percentage points in the previous Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted two weeks earlier, when Democrats had 44% support against 37% for Republicans.
However, national polls do not capture all the nuances of state-level Senate races and district-level House contests, where Republicans retain some structural advantages.
Women voters drive shift towards democrats
The widening Democratic lead was partly driven by a larger share of women saying they would vote for Democratic candidates. 
Around 50% of female voters backed Democrats, compared with 32% who said they would vote Republican.
Men also favoured Democrats, although the gap between the two parties was narrower among male voters.
Trump's popularity has suffered since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel. The war triggered a surge in gasoline prices, putting additional pressure on household finances.
The poll found that 68% of Americans disapproved of Trump's handling of the economy. The figure included 37% of respondents who identified themselves as Republicans.
When asked which party would do a better job managing the economy, 40% of respondents chose Democrats, compared with 33% who favoured Republicans.
